question: How many exact vertex-threshold queries are required to certify connectivity or separation, and when do path- or cut-based choices beat simple alternatives?
interpretation: Known-answer computational benchmark. No biological validation and no universal optimality claim. Conditional certificates are standard monotone-connectivity consequences; LazySP is a necessary baseline.
graphs: independent-set flip graphs of paths with 5 and 7 loci
standard-code leucine codon graph and its two-factor product
endpoints: Lexicographically first pair of maximum graph distance, selected without field scores. Their threshold states are forced present and never queried.
fields: graph heat-smoothed Gaussian score at median threshold
coordinate-additive Gaussian score at median threshold where binary coordinates exist
coordinate-pairwise-interaction score at median threshold where binary coordinates exist
validation_seeds: 2000 through 2049 inclusive; do not evaluate until implementation and all policy choices are frozen
initial_observations: Endpoints only, and separately a fixed 25% set selected without outcomes using a seeded permutation. Negative observations are never inferred from missingness.
policies: LazySP forward: first unqueried vertex on a shortest possible path
LazySP bisection: central unqueried vertex on a shortest possible path
path/cut alternation: alternate LazySP bisection with first unqueried member of a minimum unknown-vertex separator; known retained vertices have prohibitive capacity
tie_rule: All graph, shortest-path and min-cut inputs sorted; select lowest vertex index among tied selector candidates. Random policy uses only the frozen seed.
primary_endpoint: Number of additional vertex queries until a sound certificate; paired within identical graph, field and initial observations. Count all validation worlds, including losses and tied costs.
primary_safety_endpoint: Zero incorrect certificates against complete truth, for every query prefix in every executed case.
baselines: Report exhaustive truth, clairvoyant minimum certificate size where affordable, and exact minimax decision-tree cost for Q3 as reference bounds. A clairvoyant certificate is not an implementable prediction policy.
uncertainty: Paired differences across fixed simulated worlds; cluster summaries by graph and field family. Intervals across seeds describe this simulation design, not biological populations or arbitrary score fields.
success: All safety checks pass. Report efficiency descriptively; an algorithmic improvement requires at least 10% lower median query count than both LazySP selectors and degree selection across validation cases, without an increased worst-case query count. Otherwise retain software and report no general improvement.
failure: Any false certificate halts validation and requires a new version. Avoid tuning on validation seeds. Do not expand to costly folding measurements solely to seek a favorable result.
